SPECIFICATION FOR 
FEED ROCK SHAFT CRANK FOR SEWING MACHINES FOR 

HOUSEHOLD PURPOSES 



1- Scope — Lays down the requirements for feed rock shaft cranks for sewing machines for household 

purposes. 

2. Nomenclature — Shall be as shown in Fig. 1. 



BEARING FACE WITH 
FEED FORKED 
CONNECTION HINGE SCREW 



SMALL BOSS 





BEARING FACE 
WITH NUT 



SCREW HOLE fj ^ RGE 80$s 

FIG. 1 NOMENCLATURE FOR FEED ROCK SHAFT CRANK 

3. Material —The feed rock shaft crank shall be made from cast iron conforming to grade FG 150 of 
IS : 210-1978 ' Specification for grey iron castings ( third revision ) \ 



4. Dimensions — Shall be as shown in Fig. 2

IS : 10305 - 1982 

5. Tolerances 

5.1 The error in parallelism of the axis of the main holes of the feed rock shaft crank shall be 
within 0'3 mm per 100 mm. 

5.2 The error in the squareness of the bearing faces with respect to the main holes ^hall not 
exceed 0*3 mm per 100 mm. 

6. Workmanship and Finish 

6.1 The main holes of feed rock shaft crank shall be finished to a good finish. 

6.2 The bearing faces of the bosses of feed rock shaft crank shall be machined to a fine finish without 
any line mark. 

6.3 The casting shall be free from defects, such as cracks, flaws or blow holes and shall be chemically 
coloured or suitably plated. 

7. Marking — The feed rock shaft cranks shall be marked with manufacturer's name or trade-mark, if 
required. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution, 

8. Packing — Each feed rock shaft crank shall be given suitable anti-rust coating or wrapped in vapour 
phase inhibitor paper ( commonly khown as VPI paper ). The wrapped feed rock shaft cranks shall be 
securely packed in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each packing shall bear the 
manufacturer's name or trade-mark, the type and description of contents. 

9. Sampling 

9.1 Unless otherwise agreed between the supplier and the purchaser, the sampling plan as given in 
Appendix A shall be followed. For further information, reference may be made to IS : 2500 ( Part I )-1975 
' Sampling inspection tables : Part I Inspection by attributes and by count of defects ( first revision ) \ 



APPENDIX A 

(Clause 9.1) 
SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 

A-1. Scale of Sampling 

A-1.1 Lot — In any consignment, all the feed rock shaft cranks of the same type and manufactured from 
the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to 
constitute a lot. 

A-1 .2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements of the specification, tests shall be 
carried out for each lot separately. The number of feed rock shaft cranks to be selected at random for 
this purpose shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1. 

A-1, 3 If the feed rock shaft cranks are packed individually, in order to ensure the randomness of selection, 
IS : 4905-1968 ' Methods for random sampling ' shall be used. 

A-1. 4 If the feed rock shaft cranks are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons ( not 
less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2 ) shall be chosen at random. From 
each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of feed rock shaft cranks shall be picked 
up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of feed rock shaft cranks specified in 
col 2 of Table 1. 

A-2. Number of Tests and Criteria for Conformity 

A-2.1 The feed rock shaft crank selected according to A-1 .2 and A-1 .3 or A-1 .4 shall be examined for 
dimensions ( see 4 ), tolerances ( see 5 ), and workmanship and finish ( see 6 ). If number of feed rock 
shaft cranks failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the 
permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table 1,the lot shall be declared as conforming to the 
requirements of these characteristics. 



IS : 10305 - 1982

EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard has been prepared to unify and rationalize the types and sizes of sewing machines 
components for manufacturing in economic quantities.
